card.name: Assiko
card.tagline: Bassa guitar-and-bottle dance of hip-driven footwork
card.profile: Assiko is a popular dance and music style of the Bassa people of southern Cameroon, its name from "Assi" (earth/ground) and "Ko" (foot) (Wikipedia; African Music Library). Danced in a T-shirt and full, billowing skirt that emphasizes hip movement, its choreography uses lop-sided, gliding walks at varying heights — standing or crouching — with feats of balance and contortion. Musically it pairs a singer and guitarist with a percussionist striking an empty bottle with metal knives and forks for its crisp, metallic rhythm.
card.insight: Assiko gained popularity around the 1920s, spreading from Bassa villages to Douala and Yaoundé and beyond Cameroon; Jean Bikoko "Aladin" is regarded as the father of modern assiko and one of Central Africa's finest, under-recognized guitar masters (African Music Library).
